items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: I had played with a band out there at his Stockade, a band that had this fellow Georgetown in it -- Danny Brashears that I talked about earlier.

ctx.x: doing?" She said, "I'm not doing anything. I have a home in New Jersey." She said, "Could i sing with the trio?" I said, "Of course you can! Soon as I can find a job for us."

So I go out to try and find a job. And there was a club here, out in Maryland, on the outskirts of Sea Pleasant, Maryland, called Dikes. The fellow's name was Mr. Dikes. He had a place out there where he had this club, and he had gambling, he even had a little hotel out there, and he had a place for the summer, an outdoor place that they called the Stockade, just because he had a big fence around it, just like a stockade. He played big bands out there and all of that. I went out to see him, because for a couple…

So I knew Mr. Dikes, so he was the first one that I went to, to talk to about a job. He said, "Oh yeah, John. You can get a job here any time you like. Who have you got in your group?" I said, "Well, I got Tommy Potter, the bass player that worked with me out here. And I have Chester Brown. You know him. He used to work with Tommy Miles' band." He said, "Oh yeah, I know him." And I said, "And I've got a vocalist."
